c_coeff.description: Coefficient for function x = g(y) = c_coeff * sqrt(y)

d.description: Upper y-boundary (perfect square or clean integer)

constraints: g(y) = c_coeff * sqrt(y) >= 0 for y in [0, d]
Rotation is around the x-axis, requiring integration with respect to y
promptTemplate: Define Q as the region bounded on the right by the graph of x = {c_coeff}\sqrt{{y}} and on the left by the y-axis for y in [0, {d}]. Find the volume of the solid of revolution formed by revolving Q around the x-axis using cylindrical shells.

canonicalSolution.structure: For revolution around the x-axis using shells, the shell radius is y and the shell height (length) is g(y) = {c_coeff}\sqrt{y}. Volume V = \int_{0}^{d} 2\pi y ({c_coeff}\sqrt{y}) dy = 2\pi {c_coeff} \int_{0}^{d} y^{3/2} dy = 2\pi {c_coeff} [ (2/5) y^{5/2} ]_{0}^{d} = (4\pi {c_coeff} / 5) * d^{5/2}

hints.template: When revolving a region around the x-axis using cylindrical shells, what is the variable of integration?
The cylindrical shells are horizontal, with radius r(y) = y and length/height h(y) = g(y) = {c_coeff}\sqrt{y}. Integrate with respect to y: V = \int_{c}^{d} 2\pi y g(y) dy.
Set up the integral: V = 2\pi \int_{0}^{{d}} y ({c_coeff}\sqrt{y}) dy = 2\pi {c_coeff} \int_{0}^{{d}} y^{3/2} dy.
